question: Which lexical failures may be reported together without allowing malformed tokens into parsing?
decision: Record and aggregate recoverable single-character lexer failures while continuing to scan; raise the ordered error list before parsing. Unterminated strings record one error and stop at EOF.

recovery_limit.recoverable: lone ampersand and unexpected single characters
recovery_limit.unterminated_string: one diagnostic and stop at EOF
recovery_limit.later_stages: do not enter parser, semantic, or backend stages after any lex diagnostic list

compatibility_boundary.single_error: existing Lex message, location, source snippet, caret, exit, and stdout behavior
compatibility_boundary.direct_multi_file: all errors remap to original file paths and file-local coordinates
compatibility_boundary.import_loading: file-aware diagnostics remain ordered and parsing is skipped

rationale: Unexpected single characters do not prevent the lexer from finding later token boundaries, so recording them gives users complete diagnostics for the current input without constructing malformed tokens. Errors are raised before parsing to keep later compiler stages state-safe.
old_path_deletion_condition: Keep lexer token recovery limited to explicitly classified single-character errors until a separate decision defines multi-character malformed-token recovery and its compatibility corpus.
